 Judgment

In this appeal, the petitioners have challenged the order of dismissal of their claim petition by 4th Additional District Judge and Member, M.A.C.T., D.K., Mangalore ('the Tribunal' in short) by order dated 12.06.2014 in M.V.C. No.1479/2012.
2.
For the sake of convenience, the rank of the parties will be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

The brief facts of the case is that on 10.04.2012, at about 01:00 pm at Bantwal market, Bantwal city, on Belthangady-Bantwal road, the husband of the first petitioner, father of the petitioners No.2 and 3 by name Ravindra Bhat, the deceased, while walking by the side of road, hit by Honda Activa scooter bearing No.KA-19/EV-5706, inflicting him the injuries.
He was taken to Local Hospital at Bantwal and then shifted to Wenlock Hospital, Mangalore and thereafter to the Justice K.S. Hegde Hospital at Deralakatte (D.K.) for advanced treatment on 12.04.2012.
In spite of the treatment, the deceased succumbed to death on 15.04.2012.

The petitioners claiming that they are the dependants,
approached the Tribunal seeking award of compensation of Rs.15,00,000/-.
The claim was opposed by the Insurance Company, contending that the Honda Activa scooter was not involved in the accident and it has no liability to pay any compensation.

After recording the evidence of the parties,
the Tribunal assessed that the MFA NO.6129 OF 2014 petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.3,16,000/- under different heads, but expressed the doubt about the involvement of the Honda Smt B Rathna Bhat vs Sri K Nagesh on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7543232/
2 Activa in the accident and ultimately, dismissed the claim petition.

sentences.text: Aggrieved by the same, the petitioners have filed this appeal on various grounds.

4. Heard the arguments of Sri. U. Shivakumar, learned counsel for the appellants and Sri. B.C.
Seetharama Rao, learned counsel for the Insurance Company.
5.

It is the contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that soon after the accident, the deceased being the injured was taken to Bantwal Hospital and thereafter he was shifted to Wenlock Hospital.
Since the petitioners were busy in attending the injured, they were unable to file Police complaint on 10.04.2012 and for this reason, complaint was filed to the Police only on 11.04.2012.

PW-2 is the eyewitness, whose evidence clearly points out the MFA NO.6129 OF 2014 identification of the rider as well as the motor cycle from whom the information was passed on to the first petitioner for filing the complaint.

The death of the deceased on account of the accident has been proved beyond reasonable doubt and in spite of it, the Tribunal having assessed the compensation,
erroneously doubted the involvement of the Honda Activa and dismissed the claim.
6. Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has contended that even though the accident took place in the busy market area of Bantwal, there is a delay in filing the complaint.
There are several eye witnesses who knew the accident, but nobody have reported it to the Police for the reason that the vehicle as well as rider of the Honda Activa were not known to anybody.
In order to facilitate the petitioners to claim compensation, more than one day has taken to fix the Honda Activa and its rider.
The Tribunal has correctly doubted the involvement of the said vehicle.

The manner in which the vehicle was seized and also the MFA NO.6129 OF 2014 inspection of motor vehicle conducted clearly points out that there is a nexus between the petitioners and the Police and therefore, the petitioners cannot make a windfall for an unexpected accident in which the deceased has suffered death through unknown vehicle and supported the impugned judgment.
7. I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments advanced on both sides and also perused the materials on record.
8.
There is no dispute as to the accident that took place on 10.04.2012 at the market place of Bantwal city.

Immediately after the accident, the injured was taken to the Government Hospital,
Bantwal, Wenlock Hospital, Mangalore and thereafter to K.S. Hegde Hospital at Deralakatte (D.K.).
In any of these hospitals
, there is no specific mention of either the name of the rider or the nature of the vehicle caused the accident.
The Honda Activa first time came out after 26 and half hours of the accident.
Respondent No.1 is the rider who did not file his written statement, nor participated in the trial of the proceedings.
The first petitioner is examined as PW-1 and she has failed to offer any explanation how she came to know about the vehicle number or the details of rider.
PW-2/B. Suresh Baliga who is a shop- keeper beside the Belthangady-Bantwal road.
His evidence points out that having heard a big noise, he went and saw the deceased fallen on the road with injuries.

He saw the black coloured Smt B Rathna Bhat vs Sri K Nagesh on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/7543232/

sentences.text: Honda Activa lying with the rider at the spot.
He also spoken about spot mahazar drawn by the Police and he was also cited as a witness in C.C. No.768/2012 and he has given the evidence before the learned J.M.F.C., Bantwal.
As seen from the evidence of PWs-1 and 2 and also the records made available, it is not sufficient to infer the involvement of the Honda Activa in the accident.
10. Ex.P-5 is the statement of PW-1 recorded at Bantwal Police Station on 11.04.2012 at 04:00 pm.

In MFA NO.6129 OF 2014 this statement which is in the form of complaint, she has specifically stated that while her husband was coming towards the house, some unknown vehicle hit against her husband injuring him.
Even though this information was furnished to the Police 26 and half hours later, the details of the vehicle and the rider has not been furnished.

It is interesting to note that, in spite of PW-2 being an eye witness who saw the Honda Activa as well as the rider fallen at the spot,
he did not inform anything to the Police and in the cross- examination, he has clearly admitted that he has not reported the accident to the Police nor filed any complaint.
11.
The procedure adopted by the Investigating Officer needs a mention here.
Ex.P-6 is the second report by PW-1, reporting the death of her husband in the hospital.
In the said report, she did not mention the details of the vehicle as well as the rider.
She just referred that death of her husband occurred due to negligent driving of the scooter by its rider.
Even on MFA NO.6129 OF 2014 15.04.2012 till 04:00 p.m., the Investigation Officer did not know the details of the rider as well as the Honda Activa.
Ex.P-10 is the report submitted to the Court for adopting Section 304 of I.P.C. on 15.04.2012.

Either in Ex.P-5 or in Ex.P-6, the details of the vehicle and the rider is not made known,
but in the report submitted to the Court, the details of the vehicle number and also the rider all of a sudden found mention.
12.
It is interesting to note that on 16.04.2012 at about 10:30 a.m., the Investigating Officer conducts the seizure of the Honda Activa under Ex.P- 7/mahazar produced by its owner Suresh.

Interestingly,
on the very day at 03:30 p.m., the Motor Vehicle Inspector conducted the inspection of the said vehicle and issued the certificate at the spot under Ex.P-8, mentioning that there are no visible damage on the Honda Activa.
Contrary to this, Ex.P-7/Seizure Panchanama points out that there are scratch marks on the right side of the Honda Activa.
At 10:30 a.m., MFA NO.6129 OF 2014 the scratch mark found on the Honda Activa was visible to the Investigating Officer, but by 03:30 pm, it was not visible to the I.M.V. Inspector.
This creates the doubt about the investigation.

13. Now, coming to the history furnished in the hospital, Ex.P-11 is the discharge summary of Wenlock Hospital dated 12.04.2012, though it referred the accident on 10.04.2012, but it refers the vehicle as 'bike'.
Ex .P-18 is the discharge summary dated 15.04.2012 of K.S.Hegde Hospital which refers the history of road traffic accident before two days i.e., on 10.04.2012 at Bantwal.
P.W-2, the eye witness in the course of cross-examination has specifically admitted that the public have shifted the injured to the hospital.
He has not filed any complaint.
He admits Ex.P-2 is the deposition given by him before the learned J.M.F.C. at Bantwal in criminal case.
On perusal of the deposition, it is pertinent to note that he has not identified the accused as rider of the Honda Activa.
He denies the suggestion of the learned A.P.P. that MFA NO.6129 OF 2014 respondent No.1 was the rider of the Honda Activa and he is very much categorical that he has not at all seen the accident.
If this is worthy of the evidence of PW-2, the petitioner has to rely upon the evidence of PW-1 alone.

sentences.text: It is also her evidence before the learned J.M.F.C., Bantwal that she was not aware who has caused the accident.

Hence,
the totality of the evidence on behalf of the petitioners did clearly point out that the petitioners are not aware as to how the accident had taken place, who has caused the accident and the vehicle which involved in the accident.
All of a sudden on 15.04.2012, the Honda Activa as well as the rider first time came out from the hands of the Police.
None of the Police Officers, who have investigated the case, have been examined before the Tribunal.

Hence, though the petitioners are able to explain some accident, injuries sustained by the deceased, treatment provided to him and his death on 15.04.2012, they have failed to MFA NO.6129 OF 2014 establish the vehicle and the rider, who caused the accident.
14. I have carefully perused the impugned judgment.
The Tribunal has assessed the compensation of Rs.3,16,000/- taking into consideration the age of the deceased at 72 years.
Though the petitioners are entitled for the said compensation, who has to pay is the question.

As the petitioners have failed to establish that Honda Activa bearing No.KA-19/EB-5705 was involved in the accident and respondent No.1 was its rider, the Tribunal has rightly recorded its finding that the petitioners have not proved the involvement of the Honda Activa in question and has rightly recorded its finding that the petitioners are not entitled to claim compensation so assessed from the respondents.
Hence, I do not find any error in the reasons recorded by the Tribunal.
Hence, the appeal is devoid of merits and deserves to be dismissed.

In the result, the following:
MFA NO.6129 OF 2014 ORDER
Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed.
The impugned judgment is confirmed.
